body.rationale:
Use one new fit job per protocol on PDB 2RE9 revision 1.4 (2024-11-20), the 2.10 Å X-ray model. The verified quality summary (gxa_01m816a5h4trv9vw1s) identifies the deposited file by SHA-256 8c8b9a48cf32d0350327a8c74ecb18bec0ebacb4bdea6f484460fd7b1d5dd89b. In model 1, polymer entity 1, match label_seq_id, label_comp_id and label_atom_id across label_asym_id A, B and C. For example, all three chains begin at label position 18, LEU, with author residue number 17. Of 181 declared positions, label positions 1–17 lack observed coordinates in all three chains. Leave them unmodeled. The fixed observed-union denominator is the 164 residue identities at positions 18–181.

The inventory (gxa_01m816a52bc6m1qy7z) gives common_backbone 656 positive-occupancy N, CA, C and O correspondences and common_ca 164 positive-occupancy CA correspondences, each on all 164 residues. Their contrast isolates the contribution of the additional backbone atoms. Comparing common_backbone with ordered_backbone keeps the atom types fixed and restricts the residues to those with occupancy 1 and B_iso_or_equiv ≤40 Å² for all four atoms in each chain. This leaves 196 correspondences on 49 residues and omits 115 observed residues. LEU 18 illustrates the filter because its N has occupancy 1 in every chain, with B values of 103.51, 99.87 and 108.01 Å² in A, B and C. Compare common_ca with ordered_backbone as a combined change.

Freeze both coverage floors at the full size of the smallest verified mask, 49 residues and 49/164 of the observed union (29.878%). This admits the intended quality-filtered comparison and flags even a one-residue loss from its expected mask. The default 60-residue and 60% floors would exclude it before fitting. The 49 residues occur in all four successive 41-residue intervals of the observed sequence, with counts of 5, 11, 12 and 21. This uneven distribution limits inference to the selected sites. Verify the exact correspondence for each protocol and check that the matched coordinates determine a unique rigid fit.

For each protocol fit B onto A, C onto A and C onto B using unweighted least squares with translation and a proper rotation. Record the principal angle of the fitted rotation in degrees and the post-fit RMSD over that protocol’s matched atoms in Å. For each chain pair report all three absolute between-protocol differences for each metric and its minimum and maximum over protocols. These ranges quantify sensitivity to the three selections. RMSD can change when a filter drops residues with larger residuals even if the fitted angle changes little.

Freeze practical comparison bounds of 0.5° and 0.15 Å. A half-degree rotation displaces a point 17 Å from the axis by approximately 0.15 Å, providing a common scale for the two bounds. Independently reparse the original mmCIF, verify the selected identities and refit each pair. Require absolute reproduction errors ≤0.01° and ≤0.001 Å per fit. These allow small numerical and reporting differences while remaining 50-fold and 150-fold below the respective comparison bounds. Use unrounded fit values for decisions and report reproduction errors alongside the selection differences.

Require adequate coverage, determined fits, successful reproduction and at least two distinct comparable measurements. If a required fit or comparison is missing or fails these checks, report the overall test as insufficient and preserve every observable result and individual comparison. Carry the pairs, correspondence rules, denominator and decision criteria unchanged into subsequent rounds. The inventory supplies mask counts only for planning. All geometry measurements are prospective. The chain pairs share coordinates. B factors reflect disorder and refinement, and the filtered subset is nonrandom. A single asymmetric unit supports a sensitivity statement about these deposited coordinates. A common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding and activity require separate evidence.

interpretation.insufficient: A requested protocol lacks the frozen residue coverage, its fit is underdetermined, or fewer than two distinct comparable protocols were measured. Preserve the observable measurements and each individual comparison.
interpretation.limits: Thresholds define this coordinate sensitivity screen. Chain pairs share atoms and are dependent, and B factors mix disorder and refinement effects. A single asymmetric unit cannot establish a common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding, or activity.
interpretation.sensitive: At least one measured chain pair exceeds either comparison bound. Report all pairwise differences.
interpretation.stable: Every prespecified chain pair across every admissible measured protocol differs by at most both comparison bounds.

protocols.common_backbone: Positive-occupancy N/CA/C/O atom identities observed in all three chains.
protocols.common_ca: Positive-occupancy alpha-carbon identities observed in all three chains.
protocols.ordered_backbone: Retain a complete N/CA/C/O residue only when all four atoms on all three chains have occupancy 1 and B_iso_or_equiv <= 40 angstrom^2.

body.scope: Thresholds define this coordinate sensitivity screen. Chain pairs share atoms and are dependent, and B factors mix disorder and refinement effects. A single asymmetric unit cannot establish a common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding, or activity.

H_sensitive.reason: Ordered backbone requires all four N, Cα, C and O atoms on each of A, B and C to have occupancy 1 and B ≤ 40 Å². Its 196 matched atoms span 49 of 164 observed residues (29.878%), meeting both frozen coverage floors exactly and omitting 115 observed residues. For A–B, A–C and B–C, respectively, the absolute angle and RMSD differences for common versus ordered backbone were (0.725°, 0.615 Å), (0.117°, 1.205 Å) and (0.558°, 0.900 Å). For common Cα versus ordered backbone the differences were (0.747°, 0.595 Å), (0.077°, 1.217 Å) and (0.622°, 0.940 Å). All six ordered-backbone contrasts exceeded the RMSD bound, and both ordered-backbone contrasts for A–B and B–C also exceeded the angle bound. Across the three protocols, A–B spanned 119.421–120.168° and 0.124–0.738 Å, A–C spanned 120.113–120.229° and 0.122–1.338 Å, and B–C spanned 119.721–120.344° and 0.130–1.070 Å. Comparisons used unrounded values.

H_stable.reason: Six of the nine prespecified contrasts exceeded at least one frozen bound (0.50° or 0.15 Å), refuting the prediction that every contrast stays within both. Common backbone (656 atom correspondences) and common Cα (164) both cover 164 of 164 observed residues. Their absolute rotation-angle and RMSD differences for A–B, A–C and B–C, respectively, were (0.022°, 0.020 Å), (0.040°, 0.011 Å) and (0.064°, 0.040 Å), all within both bounds. All three protocols were admissible and reproduced their job measurements. The largest absolute differences between the job fits and the independent fits were 1.85 × 10⁻¹³° and 1.41 × 10⁻¹⁵ Å, within the frozen reproduction tolerances of 0.01° and 0.001 Å.

intent_responses.reason: I reviewed the deposited 2.10 Å X-ray mmCIF for 2RE9, revision 1.4 (2024-11-20), and confirmed the source SHA-256 8c8b9a48cf32d0350327a8c74ecb18bec0ebacb4bdea6f484460fd7b1d5dd89b against the verified source, quality inventory and all three fits. Model 1, entity 1, label chains A, B and C all begin at label position 18 (LEU, author position 17). Each first N record has occupancy 1.00, with B factors of 103.51, 99.87 and 108.01 Å², respectively. The records confirm why this residue enters the full-coverage selections and falls outside the quality-filtered selection. The exact atom identities reconstructed from the deposit matched the inventory for every protocol.
The completed coordinate-quality job and the three existing geometry jobs account for the four job submissions. The reviewer refits reproduced those observations through the independent check tool.

I reproduced all nine pair fits using Biopython SVD on the original mmCIF and checked all nine pairwise protocol contrasts against the cross-protocol evaluation. All selected atom correspondences agreed, and the centered cross-covariance matrices had positive determinants and full rank for every pair and protocol, including the 49-residue selection. The comparison measures how the fitted angles and RMSDs vary with selection within this crystal, with coverage and reproduction errors reported separately.

limitations: All three chains share the same 164 observed positions of 181 declared polymer positions. Label positions 1–17 have no coordinates in any chain, so the geometry of those positions and their effect on a fit remain undetermined.

The quality filter retains a nonrandom subset, with 5, 11, 12 and 21 residues in successive 41-residue intervals of the observed sequence. B factors reflect both disorder and refinement. RMSD is evaluated on the atoms selected by each protocol, so a lower ordered-backbone RMSD can reflect removal of sites with larger deviations as well as a change in the fitted transform.

Protocol ranges quantify selection sensitivity and the independent-fit discrepancies quantify numerical reproducibility. Coordinate and sampling uncertainty remain unestimated. The pairs share chains, and inference is confined to one deposited crystal model. A common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding and activity require separate evidence.

body.counterevidence: Changing atom type while retaining the same 164 observed residues has little effect. For common backbone (656 N, Cα, C and O correspondences) versus common Cα (164 correspondences), absolute changes in angle and RMSD are (0.022°, 0.020 Å) for A–B, (0.040°, 0.011 Å) for A–C and (0.064°, 0.040 Å) for B–C. All three meet both bounds. A–C also stays within the angle bound under both ordered-backbone contrasts despite showing the largest RMSD change. All three selections meet the coverage criteria, and the independent assessment confirms determined fits and matching atom identities for every pair.

intent_responses.reason: Used deposited 2RE9 revision 1.4 (2024-11-20), SHA-256 8c8b9a48cf32d0350327a8c74ecb18bec0ebacb4bdea6f484460fd7b1d5dd89b. The inventory, observations and independent checks identify the same input. The first modeled residue in model 1, entity 1 is LEU at label position 18 (author position 17) in chains A, B and C. Its N atoms have occupancy 1 and B factors of 103.51, 99.87 and 108.01 Å², respectively, illustrating how an observed residue can be excluded by the filter.
The inventory and three geometry jobs account for all four submissions. The independent checks reproduce the existing fits and the decision requests zero jobs.

The three selections distinguish the small effect of choosing only Cα at fixed coverage from the larger RMSD changes after filtering residues. The decision preserves the stable contrasts, quantifies pair-specific ranges and numerical agreement, and leaves the missing positions unresolved.

body.reason: Stop with the assessment of selection sensitivity. In model 1 of the 2.10 Å 2RE9 crystal structure, all nine fitted principal rotation angles are near 120°. Six of the nine prespecified comparisons exceed at least one bound (0.50° for the absolute difference in principal angle, 0.15 Å for the absolute difference in fitted RMSD). All six involve the ordered backbone. Keeping the same four backbone atom types and requiring occupancy 1 and B ≤ 40 Å² for each atom in all three chains reduces coverage from 164 to 49 residues. It lowers RMSD by 0.615 Å for B onto A, 1.205 Å for C onto A and 0.900 Å for C onto B. The corresponding absolute angle changes are 0.725°, 0.117° and 0.558°. Comparing common Cα with ordered backbone gives absolute angle and RMSD changes of (0.747°, 0.595 Å), (0.077°, 1.217 Å) and (0.622°, 0.940 Å) in the same pair order. Both contrasts exceed the RMSD bound for every pair and the angle bound for A–B and B–C. Classifications use unrounded measurements.
body.stop_reason: All three proposed atom selections have been tested and independently reproduced. The comparison at fixed residue coverage and the comparison at fixed atom types resolve the prespecified sensitivity question for the observed chains. One inventory job and three fit jobs used the four submissions, with no remaining protocol. A common-site evaluation of the different transforms would address how much of the RMSD decrease comes from changing the scoring sites. Recovering the effect of the 17 unobserved positions would require additional coordinate evidence.
body.uncertainty: Across the three selections the angle and fitted RMSD range from 119.421 to 120.168° and 0.124 to 0.738 Å for A–B, from 120.113 to 120.229° and 0.122 to 1.338 Å for A–C, and from 119.721 to 120.344° and 0.130 to 1.070 Å for B–C. These are empirical ranges over selections. Independent SVD fits agree with the original job fits to within 1.85 × 10⁻¹³° and 1.41 × 10⁻¹⁵ Å, well inside the numerical tolerances of 0.01° and 0.001 Å. The ordered selection contains 196 matched atoms on 49/164 observed residues (29.88%), exactly the coverage floor. It omits 115 observed residues and favors some parts of the sequence. B factors reflect disorder and refinement. Each protocol scores RMSD on the same sites it fits, so omitting sites with larger residuals can lower RMSD even when the angle barely changes. Label positions 1–17 of the 181 declared positions have no coordinates in any chain. Their effect on a full-chain fit is undetermined. The mmCIF gives unknown values for the overall maximum-likelihood coordinate uncertainty and Cruickshank DPI. The chain pairs share coordinates, and these measurements provide no sampling interval. Inference is confined to the deposited asymmetric unit. A common axis, solution assembly and biological activity require separate evidence.
